title: The user accepted the convention as written, with one change to the exit codes: the reserved catch-all moves to 1 so it is not sandwiched in the middle when later codes are added
Shape: workthread <area> <action> [arguments], seven areas, one per surface port, so no area name is invented
The task area sits on ForCapturingTasks
The project area sits on ForManagingProjects
The plan area sits on ForPlanningQueries, carrying today, forecast, review, and notices
The timer area sits on ForTrackingTime
The override area sits on ForOverridingRules
The capacity area sits on ForDefiningCapacity, carrying timetable and time off
The config area sits on ForConfiguring, carrying timezone, settings, and export
mcp serve sits outside an area because it is not a port operation; it hosts the agent surface and owns standard input and output
confirm <id> <code> sits outside an area because it is not a port operation; it completes a pending operation through the confirmation channel carried by ForOverridingRules
One command maps to one port operation, and the action is an imperative verb
No command exists only to reshape data the core does not produce
Output is text by default
One global --format json prints exactly one documented JSON document per invocation
--format text is the same as omitting the flag
JSON is never coloured
Text honours NO_COLOR
A command that returns no data ignores the flag silently rather than refusing it
Errors are always written to standard error
Under --format json the error is a JSON document on standard error carrying the same stable failure code the agent surface returns, plus the offending entity or field

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: Six exit codes, with the catch-all pinned low so added codes append above it

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: 0 means success

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: 1 is reserved for an unknown, internal, or uncategorised error, where the caller may still parse the output to react

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: 2 is a usage error, meaning the invocation itself is wrong

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: 3 is validation refused, meaning the input is not well formed

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: 4 is rule refused, meaning well-formed input breaks a rule, including a confirmation that was unavailable

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: 5 means the service is unreachable

section: Notes > The settled convention > Exit codes
title: The split that matters is 3 against 4: malformed input is the caller's mistake, a rule refusal is the product working as designed
Only a confirmed removal or an override may prompt, and only when standard input is a terminal
On a terminal the command prints the two-digit code and reads it back
Without a terminal the command prints the pending operation's identifier and requirement in the chosen format, exits 4, and workthread confirm <id> <code> completes it
This is the same pending-operation handshake the agent surface uses, so there is one confirmation path across surfaces, not two

section: Notes > The settled convention > Identifiers and help
title: An identifier is accepted as the bare integer or as the prefixed display form, with no fuzzy matching

section: Notes > The settled convention > Identifiers and help
title: JSON output carries both the bare integer and the prefixed display form of an identifier

section: Notes > The settled convention > Identifiers and help
title: Every command answers --help

title: --version prints the version
Shell completion is v2
Every later CLI child names its commands inside these seven areas; a new area means a new surface port, not a new prefix
Additive versions mean a command, its flags, its JSON shape, and its exit codes keep working once shipped
The JSON document per invocation is a published shape, so cli-basics fixes the envelope once, with the stable failure code and the entity fields, and the later efforts fill in the payloads
The convention is recorded on the map as a constraint naming this task, with the detail kept in this task for the architecture document to lift
